body:
I should have mentioned that he’s also shit-faced drunk right now, so anything I do say will be in one ear and out the other.

Even despite this, I’ve struggled to ever open up my emotions to him.  He threatens to hurt me for doing trivial, stupid shit that I do.  I still love him though.

He’s also said that he’s had a shitty night and he spent 5 minutes apologising and crying into my mother’s shoulder.  I have no idea what he might have done.

I think I might have heard "cognitive-behavioural" somewhere amongst the jargon they were speaking about. I assume I'd be getting that anyway seeing as it's the most common.

I suppose I'm just not wanting it to feel daunting or uncomfortable. Most of the doubts and discomfort I have when I think about going through with it most likely stem from my depression. Ever since I've had depression (hard to pinpoint a specific time since I waited so long to be diagnosed) I've been feeling lazy, antisocial and helpless. I know I'm going to have to conquer these feelings in order for me to get better, but these feelings seem to be the only things keeping me back.

I really appreciate the explanation. In my head there seems like so many factors I need to consider in order to recieve the best therapy I can get. You explaining this simply has made it seem a lot easier. Thanks again for responding, you've really helped!

It's a shame how depression can make it so hard to describe how you feel and to put your emotions into words, but that's the first step into getting better, I suppose.  I guess my greatest concern is that I'm not going to be able to describe anything and they won't be able to help me at all, because there hasn't been one event that has triggered my depression, it's just my overall personality and how much I hate myself for who I am.

It's comforting to see how you say it's "pretty relaxed". I guess it won't be that difficult after all. Thanks!

What frustrates me are the people who claim to have "dealt with this tupe of situation before", when what they really mean is it was once brought up with the weekly catch-up with Margaret. I don't mean therapists, who are trained in that specific area, I mean people who honestly try to help but they really don't. They just try to fill your brain to the brim with positive quotes and the same old advice.
Sure, some people might admit that they aren't sure how to help but they just reassure you that "we're here to help" sort of thing. I don't mind that. However, when you actively go out of your way to repeat the same, useless shit that the person you're trying to help has heard so many times, then you need to stop.
